readings.title: Moral and Civil Statutes
readings.subtitle: Laws Regarding Purity, Compassion, and Authority
readings.text: [Exodus 22:16] <dq>“And if a man entices a maiden who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he shall certainly pay the bride-price for her to be his wife.</dq> [17] <dq>“If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he pays silver according to the bride-price of maidens.</dq> [18] <dq>“Do not allow a sorceress to live.</dq> [19] <dq>“Everyone lying with a beast shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [20] <dq>“He who slaughters to a mighty one, except to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> only, is put under the ban.</dq> [21] <dq>“And do not mistreat a stranger nor oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Mitsrayim.</dq> [22] <dq>“Do not afflict any widow or fatherless child.</dq> [23] <dq>“If you do afflict them in any way, and they cry at all to <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall certainly hear their cry.</dq> [24] <dq>“And <dn>My</dn> wrath shall burn and <dn>I</dn> shall kill <dn>את</dn> you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows and your children fatherless.</dq> [25] <dq>“If you lend silver to <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people, to the poor among you, you are not to act like a lender to him. You do not lay interest on him.</dq> [26] <dq>“If you at all take your neighbor’s garment as a pledge, return it to him before the sun goes down.</dq> [27] <dq>“For that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What does he sleep in? And it shall be, when he cries to <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall hear, for <dn>I</dn> am compassionate.</dq> [28] <dq>“Do not revile <dn>Elohim</dn>, nor curse a ruler of your people.</dq> [29] <dq>“Do not delay your offering from your harvest and your vintage. Give <dn>Me</dn> the first-born of your sons.</dq> [30] <dq>“Do the same with your cattle and your sheep. Let it be with its mother seven days. On the eighth day give it to <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>“And be set-apart men to <dn>Me</dn>. And do not eat meat torn in the field, throw it to the dogs.”</dq>

readings.title: Justice and Mercy
readings.subtitle: Instructions on Integrity and Benevolence
readings.text: [Exodus 23:1] <dq>“Do not bring a false report. Do not put your hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.</dq> [2] <dq>“Do not follow a crowd to do evil, nor bear witness in a dispute so as to turn aside after many to pervert right-ruling.</dq> [3] <dq>“Also, do not show favor to a poor man in his dispute.</dq> [4] <dq>“If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall certainly return it to him.</dq> [5] <dq>“If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying under its burden, and you would refrain from helping it, you shall certainly help him with it.</dq> [6] <dq>“Do not turn aside the right-ruling of your poor in his dispute.</dq> [7] <dq>“Keep yourself far from a false matter, and do not kill the innocent and the righteous. For <dn>I</dn> do not declare the wicked right.</dq> [8] <dq>“And do not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the seeing and twists the words of the righteous.</dq> [9] <dq>“And do not oppress a stranger, as you yourselves know <dn>את</dn> the heart of a stranger, because you were strangers in the land of Mitsrayim.”</dq>

readings.title: The Sabbatical Cycles
readings.subtitle: Rest for the Land and the People
readings.text: [Exodus 23:10] <dq>“And for six years you are to sow <dn>את</dn> your land, and shall gather <dn>את</dn> its increase,</dq> [11] <dq>but the seventh year you let it rest and lie fallow, and the poor of your people shall eat. And what they leave, the beasts of the field eat. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.</dq> [12] <dq>“Six days you are to do your work, and on the seventh day you rest, in order that your ox and your donkey might rest, and the son of your female servant and the stranger be refreshed.</dq> [13] <dq>“And in all that <dn>I</dn> have said to you take heed. And make no mention of the name of other mighty ones, let it not be heard from your mouth.”</dq>

readings.title: The Three Appointed Times
readings.subtitle: The Annual Feasts of Unleavened Bread, Harvest, and Ingathering
readings.text: [Exodus 23:14] <dq>“Three times in the year you are to celebrate a festival to <dn>Me</dn>:</dq> [15] <dq>“Guard <dn>את</dn> the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you eat unleavened bread, as <dn>I</dn> commanded you, at the time appointed in the month of Abib, for in it you came out of Mitsrayim – and let none appear before <dn>Me</dn> empty-handed;</dq> [16] <dq>and the Festival of the Harvest, the first-fruits of your labors which you have sown in the field; and the Festival of the Ingathering at the outgoing of the year, when you have gathered in the fruit of your labors from the field.</dq> [17] <dq>“Three times in the year all your males are to appear before the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>“Do not offer the blood of <dn>My</dn> slaughtering with leavened bread, nor is the fat of <dn>My</dn> festival to remain until morning.</dq> [19] <dq>“Bring the choicest of the first-fruits of your land into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.”</dq>

readings.title: The Messenger and the Conquest
readings.subtitle: Promises of Guidance and Warning Against Idolatry
readings.text: [Exodus 23:20] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am sending a Messenger before you to guard you in the way and to bring you into the place which <dn>I</dn> have prepared.</dq> [21] <dq>“Be on guard before <dn>Him</dn> and obey <dn>His</dn> voice. Do not rebel against <dn>Him</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is not going to pardon your transgression, for <dn>My</dn> Name is in <dn>Him</dn>.</dq> [22] <dq>“But if you diligently obey <dn>His</dn> voice and shall do <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>I</dn> speak, then <dn>I</dn> shall be an enemy to your enemies and a distresser to those who distress you.</dq> [23] <dq>“For <dn>My</dn> Messenger shall go before you and shall bring you in to the Amorite and the Hitti and the Perizzite and the Kena’anite and the Hivvite and the Yebusite, and <dn>I</dn> shall cut them off.</dq> [24] <dq>“Do not bow down to their mighty ones, nor serve them, nor do according to their works, but you shall certainly break them down and certainly shatter their pillars.</dq> [25] <dq>“And you shall serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> shall bless <dn>את</dn> your bread and <dn>את</dn> your water. And <dn>I</dn> shall remove sickness from your midst.</dq> [26] <dq>“None shall miscarry or be barren in your land. <dn>I</dn> shall fill the number of your days.</dq> [27] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> send <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> fear before you, and <dn>I</dn> shall cause confusion among <dn>את</dn> all the people to whom you come, and make <dn>את</dn> all your enemies turn their backs to you.</dq> [28] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>את</dn> hornets before you, which shall drive out <dn>את</dn> the Hivvite, <dn>את</dn> the Kena’anite, and <dn>את</dn> the Hitti from before you.</dq> [29] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become too desolate and the beasts of the field become too numerous for you.</dq> [30] <dq>“Little by little <dn>I</dn> shall drive them out from before you, until you have increased, and you inherit the land.</dq> [31] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>את</dn> your border from the Sea of Reeds to the Sea of Philistia, and from the wilderness to the River. For <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.</dq> [32] <dq>“Do not make a covenant with them nor with their mighty ones.</dq> [33] <dq>“Let them not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against <dn>Me</dn>, to serve their mighty ones, for it is a snare to you.”</dq>

readings.title: The Covenant Confirmed
readings.subtitle: The Blood of the Covenant and the Vision of Elohim
readings.text: [Exodus 24:1] And to Mosheh <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Come up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you and Aharon, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra’el, and you shall bow yourselves from a distance.</dq> [2] <dq>“But Mosheh shall draw near to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by himself, and let them not draw near, nor let the people go up with him.”</dq> [3] And Mosheh came and related to the people <dn>את</dn> all the Words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> all the right-rulings. And all the people answered with one voice and said, “All the Words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken we shall do.” [4] And Mosheh wrote down <dn>את</dn> all the Words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and rose up early in the morning, and built a slaughter-place at the foot of the mountain, and twelve standing columns for the twelve tribes of Yisra’el. [5] And he sent young men of the children of Yisra’el, and they offered ascending offerings and slaughtered peace offerings of bulls to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] And Mosheh took half the blood and put it in basins, and half the blood he sprinkled on the slaughter-place. [7] And he took <dn>את</dn> the Book of the Covenant and read in the hearing of the people. And they said, “All that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken we shall do, and obey.” [8] And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “See, the blood of the covenant which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made with you concerning all these Words.” [9] And Mosheh went up, also Aharon, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra’el, [10] and they saw <dn>את</dn> the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, and under <dn>His</dn> feet like a paved work of sapphire stone, and like the heavens for brightness. [11] Yet <dn>He</dn> did not stretch out <dn>His</dn> hand against the chiefs of the children of Yisra’el! And they saw <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and they ate and drank.

readings.title: Moses on the Mountain
readings.subtitle: The Cloud and the Fire
readings.text: [Exodus 24:12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Come up to <dn>Me</dn> on the mountain and be there, while <dn>I</dn> give you <dn>את</dn> tablets of stone, and the Torah and the command which <dn>I</dn> have written to teach them.”</dq> [13] And Mosheh arose with his assistant Yehoshua, and Mosheh went up to the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [14] And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we come back to you. And see, Aharon and Hur are with you. Whoever has matters, let him go to them.” [15] And Mosheh went up into the mountain, and a cloud covered <dn>את</dn> the mountain. [16] And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> dwelt on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. And on the seventh day <dn>He</dn> called to Mosheh out of the midst of the cloud. [17] And the appearance of the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain, before the eyes of the children of Yisra’el. [18] And Mosheh went into the midst of the cloud and went up into the mountain. And Mosheh was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
